observations: Photo 0 shows a yellow/gold cooking gas cylinder with a protective top cage and a label; handwritten markings are visible on the side.
Photo 1 shows a blue cooking gas cylinder with a protective top cage and an oval brand logo on the body.
Photo 2 shows a top-down view of a blue cooking gas cylinder with the valve and cage visible.
The seller's text describes a single 12.5kg standard cooking gas cylinder, but the photos show at least two different cylinders (yellow and blue).

claims.evidence: No weight marking or capacity is clearly readable in any photo; two different cylinders are shown.

risks.risk: Cylinder may be damaged, rusted, or past its test/expiry date.
risks.proof: Close-up of the neck collar showing manufacture date, test date, and serial number, plus full-body photos showing rust or dents.

risks.risk: Cylinder may be empty or unable to hold gas.
risks.proof: Video showing the valve operating and gas escaping, or a weighment showing full gas weight.

risks.risk: The photos show two different cylinders (yellow and blue), so the item for sale may not match either or may be a different size.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the specific cylinder being sold with visible size and capacity markings.

proof_requests: Close-up of the cylinder collar/neck ring showing capacity, manufacture date, and last test date.
Full-body photo of the exact cylinder being sold showing condition and any capacity markings.
Video of the valve being opened to confirm it holds gas.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a cooking gas cylinder from the photos, so it can be priced at its worst case because the 12.5kg capacity and working condition are unproven.
